newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon produced 28,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon produced 28,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996.

text.p: Lebanon produced some 28,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996, topping earlier estimates by about 3,000 tonnes, the Office of Cereals and Sugar Beet said on Friday.
This compared with 26,296 tonnes produced in 1995 and 20,600 tonnes in 1994, according to the cereals office.
"We had a sugar beet crop of about 275,000 tonnes which yielded 28,000 tonnes of white sugar approximately," an official told Reuters.
He said the figures were initial estimates but the final figure was not likely to vary significantly.
The official, who in October estimated that some 25,000 tonnes of sugar would be produced in 1996, said the increase in output was mainly due to an increase in sugar content levels in sugar beet.
Lebanon imports the rest of its annual sugar reqirements of 80,000-90,000 tonnes from Cuba or the European Union.
